title: Dynamic trace estimation with access to past matrices and pointwise-in-time correctness
summary: For a fixed sequence $A_1,\ldots,A_T$, output estimates of $\tau_t=\operatorname{tr}(A_t)$ sequentially. The interface for $A_{t+1}$ becomes available only after output $\widehat\tau_t$.

model.description_zh: The matrices $A_t\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ may be nonsymmetric and indefinite. The entire sequence is fixed before the algorithmic seed is drawn. Assume $1\le p\le2$, $\|A_t\|_{S_p}\le1$, $\|A_{t+1}-A_t\|_{S_p}\le\alpha$, and $0\le\alpha<1$.

oracle.description_zh: Inputs $d,T,p,\alpha,\varepsilon,\delta$ are public. At time $t$ choose $j\le t$ and any $v\in\mathbb R^d$ to obtain exact $A_jv$. resource.description_zh:
Record the calls at every time and for every matrix and sum them to obtain $N$; one $(A_{t+1}-A_t)v$ costs two calls. This comparison uses a fixed total budget. Expected cost is a separate quantity.

Reading public inputs and exact internal arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are uncharged. The query budget is not a running-time or bit-complexity bound.

objects.definition: The matrices $A_t\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ may be nonsymmetric and indefinite. The entire sequence is fixed before the algorithmic seed is drawn. Assume $1\le p\le2$, $\|A_t\|_{S_p}\le1$, $\|A_{t+1}-A_t\|_{S_p}\le\alpha$, and $0\le\alpha<1$.
The tuple $(d,T,p,\alpha,\varepsilon,\delta)$ is public. Access becomes available sequentially at each time.

domains.definition: Return a scalar $\widehat\tau_t$ at each time. Earlier outputs cannot be supplied retrospectively after the sequence ends. No additional certificate is required.

norms.definition: Euclidean vector norm $\|z\|_2=(\sum_i|z_i|^2)^{1/2}$ and matrix operator norm $\|M\|_{\rm op}=\max_{\|z\|_2=1}\|Mz\|_2$. Define $\|M\|_{S_p}=(\sum_i\sigma_i(M)^p)^{1/p}$; settings allowing p=infinity use $\|M\|_{S_\infty}=\|M\|_{\rm op}$.

protocols.definition: At time $t$, only matrices indexed by $j\le t$ are accessible. The next matrix opens after the current estimate is returned.

comparators.definition: For a fixed sequence $A_1,\ldots,A_T$, output estimates of $\tau_t=\operatorname{tr}(A_t)$ sequentially. The interface for $A_{t+1}$ opens only after output $\widehat\tau_t$. Loss $|\widehat\tau_t-\operatorname{tr}(A_t)|$ at index $t$ has threshold $\varepsilon$. It is absolute error; norm normalization is already part of the model promise.

bracket.envelope_certificate: The upper bound applies on the general variation-budget window. The broader lower-bound claim in Theorem 5.3 cites Lemma 5.1 and Appendix D.1, which establish only a single-segment scaling reduction with $\alpha=1/(T-1)$. A matching bound over the full window requires a multisegment direct-sum argument and is not certified by this row.

evidence.supports: The DT dynamic model permits queries to all matrices that have arrived and guarantees absolute trace accuracy at each fixed time. Theorem 3.1 gives an upper bound for $p\in[1,2]$. At $p=1$, Theorem B.2 improves the second term to $T\min\{1,\alpha/\varepsilon\}H_{\alpha,\delta}$. A difference product costs two primitive calls.
notes: The DT dynamic model permits queries to all matrices that have arrived and guarantees absolute trace accuracy at each fixed time. Theorem 3.1 gives an upper bound for $p\in[1,2]$. At $p=1$, Theorem B.2 improves the second term to $T\min\{1,\alpha/\varepsilon\}H_{\alpha,\delta}$. A difference product costs two primitive calls.

evidence.supports: At $\alpha=0$, all matrices coincide. One static estimate may be reused at every time, preserving each time's guarantee.
